races.name: Loros - Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Al Wathba
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's charge holds a single run to his name — a 7f second on good ground — meaning he goes into this with directly relevant experience; racing slightly outside his natural role as a prominent type rather than a pure leader, his front-running mandate in a tiny field is essentially handed to him by default, though the style-fit tag should temper confidence slightly.

runners_data.name: Ebt's Warrior
runners_data.note: A William Muir & Chris Grassick debutant with no public form to assess, carrying the going-unknown flag as a consequence; his lighter schedule and absence of a form string mean his pace preferences are genuinely uncertain, and while he is mapped to the rear due to field composition, he should not be assumed a natural hold-up horse — his actual position in running may be closer to mid-division.

runners_data.name: Jimtrott
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's juvenile has two placed efforts at 6f on good and soft ground, suggesting he handles cut but will now need to see out an extra furlong on faster terrain; Charles Bishop takes the ride 38 days after his last run, and stepping up in trip on quicker going represents an unproven combination, though his prominent style suits the expected race shape if his stamina holds.

races.paceDynamic: Al Wathba is the sole confirmed pace-setter here and, with only two rivals in a three-runner field, will lead comfortably into the 7f trip on good-to-firm ground without any rival capable of pressing him. Jimtrott holds a prominent style and may track Al Wathba closely through the early stages, but with no horse genuinely looking to take on the leader, the fractions should be controlled and metronomic. Ebt's Warrior, redistributed to the rear of this small field, is not a natural hold-up type and will likely sit closer than the mapping implies once the race develops in real time. The race shape strongly favours the lead-and-dictate profile — a single front-runner setting a sustainable, uncontested pace on fast ground at 7f rewards horses who can bowl along and resist the challenge, making prominent-to-leading runners the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Al Wathba Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Al Wathba leads unchallenged and dictates a comfortable gallop, gradually extending the margin through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Al Wathba has already demonstrated ability at 7f on good ground (runner-up on sole start) and with Charlie Appleby's operation behind him, an uncontested lead on a flat track suits him ideally; no rival has the profile or mandate to peg him back early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Jimtrott tracks tightly and puts Al Wathba under genuine pressure from halfway, turning it into a two-horse duel.
scenarios.body: Eve Johnson Houghton's Jimtrott has been placed twice at shorter trips and stepping up to 7f may unlock more stamina, allowing him to sustain a challenge; if Al Wathba's lead is contested, both prominent-style horses slug it out and the stronger stayer prevails.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Ebt's Warrior Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and Ebt's Warrior, sitting last, produces a late run to catch the tiring leaders.
scenarios.body: Ebt's Warrior is an unknown quantity on debut and his redistribution to the rear reflects tactical necessity rather than natural style, so any late finish depends on the front-runners tying each other up; in a three-runner race that scenario is unlikely but cannot be fully dismissed on debut.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Flat Finish — Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If good-to-firm ground rides quicker than expected and all three runners are tested for stamina over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated surface could stretch the pace so that no one horse finishes strongly, leaving the race decided by the one with the deepest reservoir of stamina; with Jimtrott having form over shorter trips and Ebt's Warrior unknown, Al Wathba's Appleby preparation may prove the deciding factor.

watchPoints.text: Al Wathba leads unchallenged — watch whether he finds a true gallop or dawdles, as a falsely-run race over 7f could compress the finish and undermine his positional advantage.
Jimtrott's stamina over 7f on good-to-firm is unproven after two placed runs at 6f on softer surfaces — watch whether he fades inside the final furlong if the pace is even slightly honest.
Ebt's Warrior is a debut runner with no sectional or style data — watch the market moves at the off and his early positioning, as either could reveal trainer intelligence not visible in the form.

With only three runners, any early incident or stumble at the start could dramatically reshape the race — watch the break closely, particularly from Al Wathba who must secure the lead to fulfil his expected role.

races.name: Catalogue Engineering Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Love Rome
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner, Cieren Fallon in the saddle adds confidence from a Charlie Johnston yard that has placed five of 42 runners in the past fortnight; two runs over seven furlongs on good, both placed, and the uncontested lead on good-to-firm is exactly what she needs.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked last on our figures, Love Rome faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and those back-to-back placed efforts at least suggest some consistency.

runners_data.name: Greek Symphony
runners_data.note: Won over seven furlongs at Sandown on fast ground last time, Mason Paetel claims 5lb, and Oliver Cole's 3/15 trainer strike-rate is modest but this is her most suitable race shape yet given she naturally tracks the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Greek Symphony arrives in fine nick, winning last time out and placing in each of her last three starts, with experience over today's trip and going. Carrying 132 lb from stall 2, she looks the one to beat, though the weight asks a question.

runners_data.name: Bayside
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who was a beaten favourite last time at Goodwood, Rod Millman's yard is in modest form, and a 38-day break adds a mild query; all three recent runs on good or similar have returned minor placings at best, and this pace shape is unlikely to bring her into the race until too late.|
runners_data.comment: Bayside showed a third last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, with our rating of 80 marking her out as a leading threat from stall 3; the main danger is that her two unplaced efforts in recent starts suggest consistency remains a question.

runners_data.name: Katie's Cavalier
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is a significant booking but the form string of 5664 is uninspiring, David Loughnane's yard is winless from 16 runners over the past fortnight, and while she naturally races prominently, she has not converted that position into a result in four outings.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Katie's Cavalier nevertheless brings strong distance experience and races fresh off a 15-day break carrying 127 lb from stall four — our rating of 74 suggests he's ahead of his official mark. The risk is that his recent finishes make it hard to pinpoint a breakthrough.

runners_data.name: Better Nature
runners_data.note: Consistent over seven furlongs on good ground with back-to-back runner-up finishes in that context, Rob Hornby fits well in the saddle, and Jonathan Portman's operation is quietly ticking; she is the most credible late threat if anything goes wrong up front, but she needs a stronger gallop than Love Rome is likely to set.|
runners_data.comment: Better Nature is winless in his last three starts, though he has shown some ability with a third two starts back and a second last time out; he has run over today's trip and going, but with our figures placing him fifth of six, it is hard to make a strong case.

runners_data.name: Jazzy Bay
runners_data.note: In-form with three consecutive placings, Eve Johnson Houghton's yard has been active, but she is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural rear-tracking style is squeezed by the number of closers in this field — racing out of role in a position closer to midfield than she would prefer, her ability to produce a decisive finish is compromised by the lack of truly fast early fractions.|
runners_data.comment: Jazzy Bay has been knocking on the door, third three of his last five starts, and arrives here fit on just 12 days' rest with experience of today's trip and conditions — the concern is he remains winless and has yet to convert that consistency into a win.

races.paceDynamic: Love Rome is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should secure a comfortable, uncontested position from the outset and control tempo on good-to-firm ground over seven furlongs at Leicester. Greek Symphony and Katie's Cavalier are the prominent types most likely to track closely in second and third, but neither has the profile to seriously pressure Love Rome for the lead, meaning the pace is likely to be sustainable and even — a classic front-runner's setup. Jazzy Bay is a true hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map because there are more closers in this field than the pace shape can accommodate at the rear; she is unlikely to get her natural late position and her tactical scenario is consequently discounted. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit prominently or lead, as the controlled tempo will not generate the sustained finish pace that genuine hold-up horses need to reel in a front-runner who has had it easy through the early and middle stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Love Rome Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Love Rome breaks cleanly and dictates a comfortable, uncontested gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Love Rome sets a manageable pace with Greek Symphony and Katie's Cavalier tracking at a respectful distance, and she has enough in hand at the weights to repel any challenge from the two furlong pole home on this good-to-firm surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Greek Symphony or Katie's Cavalier track aggressively and wear Love Rome down in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The tempo stays honest but the closeness of the tracking pair to the leader means any slight error or fade from Love Rome becomes decisive, with Greek Symphony's recent winning form over seven furlongs making her the chief beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely hot and the field strings out, allowing a late-running horse to pick off tired rivals.
scenarios.body: Better Nature, who has placed twice over seven furlongs on good ground and is trained in-form, is the most credible closer here given her natural style; Jazzy Bay's redistribution means she is unlikely to get far enough back to produce her trademark late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Tactically
scenarios.trigger: If there is a significant incident, stumble, or Love Rome is slowly away and the field bunches chaotically.
scenarios.body: Without a controlling leader the race becomes a sprint from two furlongs out, suiting any runner with tactical speed regardless of form; Bayside's varied experience and Jazzy Bay's consistent placing ability could see them involved.

watchPoints.text: Love Rome's start is critical — if Cieren Fallon gets her away cleanly she is highly likely to control this race from front to finish; watch for her barrier manners.|
Greek Symphony is the most likely beneficiary if Love Rome weakens, having won over the same trip on similarly fast ground; Mason Paetel's 5lb claim keeps the weight competitive.|
Jazzy Bay's redistribution means she may end up racing in an unnatural midfield spot — if she is pushed forward by her jockey to compensate, she could compromise her finishing effort entirely.|
The going is reported as Good to Firm for this race specifically, which suits the prominently-run shape and may be a concern for Bayside, whose only win came on soft ground.|

Katie's Cavalier's trainer David Loughnane is winless from 16 runners in the past 14 days — in a race where her form reads 5664, the yard's current lack of firepower makes an upgrade in finishing position harder to project.|

races.name: TLC Teddies For Loving Care Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Robusto
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's six-year-old has prominent-racing tendencies and returns from a 29-day break wearing a hood; his one win in similar going came over 15f and he has shown the ability to track a front-runner and stay on, making his place claims solid, though a mark of 65 and an apprentice claim with Harry Vigors (5) are relevant context.
runners_data.comment: Robusto shaped well when third last time out, and a winner four starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; the 140 lb burden is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Ottoman
runners_data.note: Oliver Greenall and Josh Guerriero's four-year-old is, by instinct, a horse who settles at the back and produces his effort late — he has two wins and six places in similar going — but with the hold-up section of this small field crowded, he is shown in midfield on the map; racing out of his natural role carries a genuine discount to his chance, and a trainer who has gone 0/5 in the last 14 days adds a note of caution.
runners_data.comment: Ottoman has won once in his last six starts, with two fifths bracketing that success, and ranked last on our figures he's a difficult proposition to support. He has run over today's trip and going, and 15 days since his last run leaves him fit enough.

runners_data.name: Mountbatten
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old is the race's sole natural front-runner; he won over 12f at Sandown last time and steps back up to 14f here — the extra distance over good-to-firm on a flat track suits his relaxed style perfectly, and with no rival willing to fight for the lead he should get an uncontested, race-controlling position from gate to wire.
runners_data.comment: Mountbatten won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is that his last outing ended in a fourth, and he has to shoulder 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Barak Warrior
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride on James Keane's lightly-raced three-year-old, whose only win came over 12f on firm ground at Carlisle last time; he is a hold-up type stepping up to 14f for the first time and with only four career runs his profile is thin — the good-to-firm ground suits but he is unproven at this trip and over a distance that demands a thorough test of stamina.
runners_data.comment: Barak Warrior arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a serious contender here; the main risk is whether 39 days off has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Al Maslool
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends out this three-year-old with Cieren Fallon aboard, a high-class combination that commands respect; he has won over 12f on good going and placed three times at the same trip, and while he is a hold-up type who will need something to go wrong up front, his class edge and the Haggas 10/49 14-day strike rate suggest he is in form and capable of making a bold bid if the race develops in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Al Maslool catches the eye on the back of a win last time out, and he has run over today's distance and going before; the 15-day turnaround looks sharp enough, and carrying 133 lb is the one query against a lightly progressive profile.

runners_data.name: Sahm Naif
runners_data.note: James Horton's three-year-old has won twice over a mile and a quarter on good ground and now faces a career-best trip of 1m4f; he is a natural presser who will want to sit just off the pace, and his light weight of 129lbs and improving form string (-74115) suggest this step up in trip could unlock more — the unknown is whether the extra two furlongs stretches him.
runners_data.comment: Beaten fifth last time out dampens enthusiasm for Sahm Naif, and his speed rating of 58 leaves him well short of what's required ranked fifth of six on our figures; he has gone experience and two wins in his last five starts to his name, but he's hard to fancy here.

races.paceDynamic: Mountbatten is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a field of six over 1m4f on good-to-firm ground at Leicester, he should stride out unchallenged and set a sustainable, controlled tempo from the outset. Robusto and Sahm Naif are the natural prominent types who will look to track close behind, giving the race a clear shape: one horse on the engine, two in close attendance, and the remainder coming from further back. The hold-up contingent of Barak Warrior, Al Maslool, and the redistributed Ottoman will need either the pace to quicken sharply or Mountbatten to fold to launch a telling late run — neither outcome is guaranteed when the fractions are dictated at will. This race shape strongly favours horses who race prominently or can at least press from second or third, as a steady-to-moderate gallop set by a relaxed front-runner leaves little room for closers to make up meaningful ground late on; the field holds more hold-up types than can realistically get to the front, and with Ottoman a true hold-up horse mapped forward only through redistribution, the rear-division advantage is further diluted.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mountbatten Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mountbatten bowls along in front at his own tempo and the prominent horses behind him cannot sustain enough pressure to force a truly searching pace.
scenarios.body: Mountbatten dictates every fraction, reaches the home straight with reserves intact, and only those travelling close to him throughout have any realistic chance of pegging him back; a tactical crawl-then-quicken plays entirely to the strengths of the leader and those racing in his slipstream.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Apply Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Robusto and Sahm Naif both push forward aggressively early and collectively raise the gallop enough to stretch the field.
scenarios.body: A faster, more genuine pace tests Mountbatten's stamina and opens the race up for hold-up horses to close, but those riding prominently who conserve energy best through the middle stages remain best placed at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses turning for home and the closers find genuine daylight to launch coordinated runs from the rear.
scenarios.body: Al Maslool, with course form and a good jockey booking in Cieren Fallon, is best equipped to time a late run, while Barak Warrior's recent winning form over 12f on firm gives him some claims; however, this scenario is undermined by Ottoman being a true hold-up type who is unlikely to secure a clean stalking position and therefore cannot be relied upon as a closer here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Turns Tactical Mess
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for position disrupts the anticipated shape and the race is run in fitful bursts rather than at any consistent rhythm.
scenarios.body: An uneven gallop unsettles horses with a clear positional preference and opens the door for an opportunist, though with only six runners such chaos is unlikely; any runner able to switch off and quicken late from a handy pitch stands to benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Mountbatten's ability to set a truly uncontested gallop is the single biggest determinant of race shape — watch whether Robusto or Sahm Naif press Dylan Hogan for the lead in the opening furlong, as any sustained challenge for the front could significantly alter pace fractions and open the race up.

Al Maslool's draw and early positioning will be critical — Cieren Fallon needs a clean break and clear passage turning for home, and if he gets boxed in behind a slow-moving pack in a small field the hold-up style could become a liability rather than an asset.

Ottoman's redistribution to midfield on the map signals that he is racing out of his natural hold-up role; watch whether Jack Callan elects to drop him back to his preferred position regardless, which would leave him needing a much more demanding pace than Mountbatten is likely to set.

Sahm Naif is unproven beyond 10f and steps up significantly in trip — watch whether Ray Dawson settles him in the first half of the race, as any early exuberance on unfamiliar ground could leave him empty in the final two furlongs where the race is likely to be decided.

The going report confirms good-to-firm conditions for the 3:34, firmer than the nominal GOOD tag — horses wearing headgear (Robusto: hood; Mountbatten: hood; Al Maslool: hood; Sahm Naif: hood) may react differently to the faster surface, and any horse showing signs of being unsettled early on good-to-firm deserves attention.

races.name: Dave Myers Memorial - I'm Having A Dave Day Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Cancelled
runners_data.note: Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill runner wearing tp (tongue-tie/plate combination) who returns after just 11 days, a quick turnaround that can signal stable confidence; holds a win over 8f on Good ground and her sim-going record of 11/15 is the strongest in the field, but her hold-up style means she needs a genuine pace to chase down.
runners_data.comment: Cancelled arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, making her a strong threat at the weights; the worry is whether she can back it up on just 11 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Venetian Sky
runners_data.note: William Haggas, whose 10/49 fourteen-day figures confirm consistent use of form, sends this lightly-raced three-year-old back to 8f after a series of 7f runs; her sim-going record on Good is limited (3 runs) but the step to a mile and a better draw-position from the back may unlock more; natural hold-up style is genuine and not a redistribution artefact.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Venetian Sky has been knocking on the door with a pair of fourth-place finishes and a third in that sequence, but her ranking at the foot of these five on our figures makes her hard to fancy, despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Spiritoftheblues
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's filly is flagged with a STYLE_FIT caution (0.92) as a prominent racer who may find the lone-leader role slightly outside her comfort zone; she has placed consistently (1W4P in similar going across six runs) and her recent 11-day return suggests readiness, but if she is pressed to lead alone she may be setting herself up for rivals.

runners_data.name: Kaori
runners_data.note: George Boughey's three-year-old sports the hood (p headgear) and has a tidy placed record at 7-8f on Good, giving her solid course-type credentials; her natural prominent style means she should travel smoothly in second and get first crack at the leader, making her the most straightforward beneficiary if Spiritoftheblues ties up.
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and again four starts back, Kaori has run over today's trip and going and arrives here in decent nick just 18 days after her last outing — though she remains winless in recent starts, and that elusive breakthrough is the main question mark against her.

runners_data.name: Tamzan
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's filly has a strong underlying profile — a win over 8f on Good and four placings in the last five — and the trainer's 1/7 recent strike rate is eye-catching; she is a genuine hold-up horse whose position on the pace map is a redistribution artefact, meaning she will race from the back rather than midfield, and STYLE_FIT (0.93) tempers confidence in scenarios that require her to operate closer to the pace.
runners_data.comment: Tamzan arrives here fit and in form, with a win two starts back and third last time out showing she's operating consistently at this level — she's run over today's trip and going, and off 26 days looks ready to go. The main worry is that our rating ranks her fourth of five runners.

races.paceDynamic: Spiritoftheblues is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no rival likely to contest the lead aggressively, she should dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo around Leicester's flat mile. Kaori is the only other prominent-style runner and is more likely to track than challenge for the lead, meaning the fractions will be set by one horse without meaningful pressure. The remaining trio — Cancelled, Venetian Sky, and Tamzan — are all hold-up types by nature, though Tamzan is a redistributed runner who, as a true hold-up horse, is unlikely to secure the midfield slot the map assigns and will race further back than shown. A single uncontested front-runner setting a measured pace on Good to Firm ground over a flat mile creates a race that fundamentally favours closers with a sharp turn of foot — hold-up horses who can produce a sustained late run into the straight — provided the pace is honest enough to see them home, which one sole leader at this level is not guaranteed to provide.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Spiritoftheblues Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Spiritoftheblues leads throughout at a controlled tempo and the hold-up horses cannot generate enough momentum from the back.
scenarios.body: Spiritoftheblues dictates every yard at a modest gallop on fast ground, and the small field means no rival can manufacture a stronger pace to stretch her; she conserves energy and quickens when challenged entering the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften Spiritoftheblues and the closers produce decisive late runs.
scenarios.body: Cancelled, with the most experience at the trip and solid similar-going form, and Venetian Sky, handled by William Haggas whose runners carry intent fresh at this grade, both have the class to finish powerfully if the front-runner has done enough work.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Kaori Outstays From Tracking
scenarios.trigger: If Kaori settles just behind Spiritoftheblues, produces a smooth challenge two furlongs out and the hold-up runners fail to close.
scenarios.body: Kaori's consistent placed form at shorter trips suggests she handles pace-pressure well, and a front-two tactical scenario suits a horse whose headgear (p) indicates she can race alertly and maintain concentration over a mile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tamzan Lands The Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Tamzan's trainer sends her forward of her natural position and she capitalises on the compressed small-field shape with a well-timed run.
scenarios.body: Tamzan won over 8f on Good ground and Tregoning's 1/7 fourteen-day strike rate is a lively stat, but her true hold-up profile means this scenario requires her to race against type or find the pace unexpectedly collapse; the probability is low precisely because the redistribution signals that role is compromised.

watchPoints.text: Spiritoftheblues — watch whether she is allowed to dictate without pressure; if Kaori pushes her early, the tempo could quicken sharply and flip the race entirely in favour of closers like Cancelled and Venetian Sky.

Tamzan — her true running position will be from the rear, not midfield as mapped; if the pace is slow she could find herself with too much to do in a short straight and the redistribution effectively removes her from the outcome of SCENARIO_A.

Cancelled — the 11-day turnaround is sharp; watch the market for signs the O'Neill yard are running her fit versus simply active, as her entire chance depends on a pace strong enough to reel in a front-runner she will be racing well off.

Venetian Sky — stepping from 7f to 8f for the first time on turf (her Stall/AW run over 8f doesn't fully count); watch whether she settles cleanly for Fallon, as any greenness over the extra furlong could cost her the late run her hold-up style requires.

Going confirmation is Good to Firm for this race despite the header listing Good — fast conditions suit a front-runner gaining an uncontested lead even more than standard Good, reinforcing Spiritoftheblues' positional advantage.

races.name: ADS Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ray Mon Dough
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance last time on Good ground and is the most credible of the two front-runners here; at 15 days since that win Oliver Cole keeps him fresh, though he has been beaten when losing his front-running role and faces a direct speed duel from Percy's Star throughout.
runners_data.comment: Ray Mon Dough has finished sixth in two of his last three starts, and though a runner-up two starts back offers some encouragement, he ranks fifth of six on our figures and his speed rating gives little cause for optimism at these weights.

runners_data.name: Art Lover
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner with Cieren Fallon riding who has a solid recent second on similar Good ground and a win on Soft, suggesting he handles cut but handles quick too; sits at the back of the field naturally and needs the leaders to do enough work to bring him into it late over this 6f trip.
runners_data.comment: Art Lover ran a cracking race last time out, finishing second, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions — his main danger is that two indifferent runs before that return to form may hint at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Evening Blues
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner who has placed three times on Good ground in five such starts and brings Ben Robinson for the modestly-placed Hanlon yard; dropped back from 7f-9f trips recently and the return to 6f is the key unknown, though the form at this trip earlier in the season was solid.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but **Evening Blues** shaped with real promise when second two runs back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions — his rating of 101 puts him clear of these, and at 137 lb from stall four he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Sea Cookie
runners_data.note: The most interesting pace angle in the race — two recent wins on Good ground at 6f and a prominent style that can slot just off the leaders; Tom Clover's yard is 4/21 over the last 14 days suggesting reasonable current form, though the horse is 0 from its last five runs in the form string which needs reconciling against those course-and-distance victories.
runners_data.comment: Sea Cookie arrives on the back of back-to-back wins two and three starts back, has experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 90 puts him ahead of his official mark — the unplaced effort last time out is the one thing to overcome.

runners_data.name: Nuevo Slovo
runners_data.note: 69 days off the track is a flag for a horse whose trainer Simon Pearce has sent out only one runner in 14 days, and while Nuevo Slovo's sole win came over 5f on Good ground the step up to 6f has produced finishes of 7th and 6th; Paddy Bradley will likely sit in midfield or hold up and needs a strong pace to compensate for the layoff.
runners_data.comment: Nuevo Slovo brings distance-and-going experience and a useful ratings edge over his mark, and that win in his last five starts shows the ability is there — the concern is a sequence of unplaced efforts since, and 69 days off will need to be shaken off quickly.

runners_data.name: Percy's Star
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is a significant booking for this OR-74 runner who won over 5f and placed at 6f on Good ground recently; she will race prominently or lead alongside Ray Mon Dough and the pace battle she creates is arguably more important to the race shape than her own winning chance, though De Sousa's ability to manage that duel could keep her competitive.
runners_data.comment: Percy's Star has won in recent starts — a winner two starts back — but sixth last time out leaves him hard to fancy as the lowest-rated runner in the field; he has run over today's trip and going before, which at least counts in his favour.

races.paceDynamic: Ray Mon Dough and Percy's Star are both confirmed front-runners, and with just six runners over a flat 6f at Leicester on Good to Firm ground, these two will press each other from the stalls, creating a genuinely contested early pace rather than a solo soft lead. Ray Mon Dough has won over this course and distance and brings the higher recent form, while Percy's Star has De Sousa aboard and a win over 5f suggesting she'll want to push on rather than surrender ground. The resulting honest gallop on quick ground over a straight six sets up a race where the pace is real but not suicidal — neither leader is so dominant that they'll steal a canter. This shape marginally favours prominent racers who can track just off the duel and pounce in the final furlong, with hold-up horses needing a strong enough fractions to generate the gap they require; the field is compact enough that Sea Cookie and Evening Blues, sitting just off the pace, are the profiles most likely to benefit from the leaders pressing each other into the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leaders Battle, Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Ray Mon Dough and Percy's Star press each other genuinely through the first half, setting an honest fractions that begins to tell approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The two leaders exhaust each other's reserves while a horse travelling smoothly in third or fourth tracks into the straight with a clear run and cuts them down late; Good to Firm ground rewards those who conserve energy through the middle portion rather than burning it at the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two leaders — most likely Ray Mon Dough — gets a soft end to the early duel and finds the other backing off, allowing a controlled solo lead from the halfway point.
scenarios.body: With the pace regulated and no sustained pressing in the back straight, the leader gets into a rhythm and simply has too much ground to make up on; a flat track with quick ground offers no hiding place for closers who need a strong pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace between Ray Mon Dough and Percy's Star is genuinely fierce and the leaders tie each other up completely before the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: The fractions collapse the leading duo leaving hold-up horses Art Lover and Nuevo Slovo with daylight to close into; Cieren Fallon's positional intelligence on Art Lover becomes a significant asset if the finish truly opens up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Fizzles, Messy Race
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner commits fully and the early gallop is slower than expected, creating a muddled tactical affair at 6f.
scenarios.body: A lack of rhythm causes the field to bunch approaching the straight, producing a wide-open scramble where positional luck and draw matter as much as ability; this scenario is unlikely given two genuine speed horses in the line-up.

watchPoints.text: Ray Mon Dough and Percy's Star will fight for the early lead — watch whether either blinks in the first furlong, because whoever controls the pace dictates the entire race shape.

Sea Cookie's form string shows 0 wins from the last five runs yet includes two recent 6f wins on Good — check whether those wins are current-season form or earlier; if the horse is returning to form this is a major player, if the string reflects a slide it is not.

Nuevo Slovo is 69 days absent with a trainer who has sent out only one runner in the past fortnight — monitor the market move and paddock condition, as a flat-track 6f on quick ground gives little margin for a horse not fully tuned.

Art Lover holds a healthy record on similar going (four runs, two places) but Cieren Fallon will need a genuinely strong pace from the front-runners to manufacture a winning run from off the pace over this trip — if the pace is modest, the hold-up position becomes a liability.

races.name: Leicestershire And Rutland Freemasons Charity LRFC Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Pisanello
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins on good ground over 8f-9f, now at 9 years old but in the form of his life — visored, and Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim brings the weight down attractively; hold-up horse ideally suited to a slow-run sprint finish and the step back to 10f here should not inconvenience him given his recent turf form.
runners_data.comment: Pisanello arrives in cracking form, winning three of his last six starts including his last three on the bounce, and he has experience of today's trip and going. Carrying 141 lb from stall one, he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Ricardo Phillips
runners_data.note: Trainer Henry Candy sends him in sound form (2/9 in 14 days), but the key context is that his natural hold-up style means he will front-run only by necessity — any pace he sets will be measured, and his true finishing effort may arrive later than his map position suggests; 135lbs and 18 days since last run are manageable.
runners_data.comment: Ricardo Phillips arrives here in solid nick — third two starts back and runner-up last time out, he has experience over today's trip and going, and 18 days is a sharp enough turnaround. The risk is that his rating leaves him vulnerable to the top-rated runner.

runners_data.name: Kameel
runners_data.note: Jessica Macey's four-year-old has finished fourth in three of his last four on good ground at 10f-12f — consistent but unable to win — and while he wears a hood, his true rear-of-field style is compressed into a midfield slot here, meaning he will need a stronger gallop than Ricardo Phillips is likely to provide to deliver his best effort.
runners_data.comment: Kameel has been knocking consistently on the door, posting a second four starts back and three fourths in his last six, returning fit on 18 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going; the chief concern is he's yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Hachiman
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's gelding steps up in trip having placed three times in ten-runner fields over 10f on good ground, but his record beyond 10f in soft or standard going is poor; his genuine hold-up style is shuffled forward into midfield on the map, and the likely steady pace is the opposite of what he needs to produce a late run.
runners_data.comment: Hachiman shaped with promise when third two starts back and returns here fit on 18 days' rest, having experience of today's trip and conditions — our rating of 59 suggests he holds a solid chance. The main concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Clipsham Noble
runners_data.note: Two wins from five runs on good ground at 10f-12f give him a solid profile for today's conditions, and Liam Wright's 5lb claim brings his 131lbs down to a competitive weight; a patient-racing type forced into a midfield map position, his form figures on this going (8/15, 2W3P) are the second-strongest in the field and he holds each-way claims in a sprint finish.
runners_data.comment: Clipsham Noble won last time out but was sixth two starts back and has looked inconsistent in recent starts, leaving him hard to fancy on our figures here; experience over today's trip and going, plus draw two, are the main positives.

runners_data.name: Read All About It
runners_data.note: Returning after 78 days off for the Muir & Grassick yard, who have hit 3/19 in the last 14 days — the layoff is the primary concern, and his form on turf (only one placed effort from four turf runs on similar going) is uninspiring; a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield, he would need a strong pace and peak fitness to threaten.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Read All About It is hard to fancy after 78 days off; a third three starts back and experience over today's trip and going are the only crumbs of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Ricardo Phillips is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this six-runner field, redistributed to the front because no natural front-runner exists — his true style is hold-up, meaning the pace he sets will be measured and controlled rather than pressured or genuine, creating a falsely-run, strung-out gallop over the 1m2f on good-to-firm Leicester ground. With no horse capable of genuinely pushing him from the front, the fractions are likely to be even and conservative in the first half of the race, leaving a strong premium on the ability to quicken off a slow pace in the straight. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses with a sharp turn of foot who can travel prominently or switch on late — notably Pisanello, who has been in scintillating recent form over similar trips and going, and Clipsham Noble, whose course-and-distance profile aligns well. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Kameel, Hachiman, Clipsham Noble and Read All About It are all genuine hold-up horses shuffled forward on the map; Pisanello is most likely to command its natural position and exploit the modest pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Quicken
scenarios.trigger: If Ricardo Phillips sets a conservative tempo unchallenged, bunching the field and triggering a sprint finish in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The controlled gallop plays into the hands of horses with a genuine finishing kick, and those who have settled near the pace without expending energy will have most left to give.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Kick Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Ricardo Phillips and Pisanello both travel prominently and kick decisively from two furlongs out, leaving the hold-up horses with too much to do.
scenarios.body: A front-two breakaway on this flat track becomes near-impossible to reel in late when the closers are stuck racing out of their natural hold-up role.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to string the field out and genuine hold-up horses get a strong gallop to aim at in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Kameel or Hachiman would need the race run to suit their true rear-of-field style, but given Ricardo Phillips is not a natural front-runner, the required gallop is unlikely to materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, No Clear Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Ricardo Phillips declines to lead and the field idles in a muddled group with no horse willing to commit, creating a race decided by luck and position.
scenarios.body: A truly pace-less affair over 1m2f on a flat track becomes a lottery, with the most experienced jockey or widest-drawn horse potentially stealing it on the nod.

watchPoints.text: Pisanello's recent hat-trick of wins on good ground at similar trips makes him the form anchor — watch whether Conor Whiteley slots him in behind Ricardo Phillips immediately and times his run, as any delay in finding clear air in a six-runner sprint finish could cost him.

Ricardo Phillips is not a natural front-runner — watch the first furlong to see if he genuinely commits to the lead or drifts back, because if he fails to lead, this race could collapse into a slow-motion crawl that unsettles all tempo-dependent runners.

Clipsham Noble is the most interesting hold-up horse in the field given his two wins on this ground over this trip — watch whether Liam Wright (5) can find cover early and position him to challenge in the final two furlongs rather than getting stranded wide.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race despite the headline card showing Good — the faster surface rewards horses with a clean action and penalises those who need cut, so watch for any pre-race market moves reflecting ground suitability concerns.

With five of six runners returning from 18+ days off (and Read All About It off 78 days), fitness is a collective question — watch the paddock for any horses who look less than fully wound up, as the trainer strike-rates suggest some are better-prepared than others.
